Industry News: Seth Rogen Reveals “Bad Dynamic” on Dawson’s Creek During Guest Role

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2164 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eonline

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Studio star admitted that he had a less than stellar time guest starring on Dawson’s Creek in 2003, adding he felt some tensions among the cast and crew.
  • “I hated that,” Rogen confessed on the Nov.
  • The 44-year-old explained that he was convinced to appear on the season six episode “Rock Bottom” by his former Freaks and Geeks costar and Dawson’s Creek actress Busy Philipps after she appeared on his show Undeclared.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Seth Rogen couldn’t wait for this gig to be over.

The Studio star admitted that he had a less than stellar time guest starring on Dawson’s Creek in 2003, adding he felt some tensions among the cast and crew.

“I hated that,” Rogen confessed on the Nov. 16 episode of the Happy Sad Confused podcast. “That was not fun.”.

The 44-year-old explained that he was convinced to appear on the season six episode “Rock Bottom” by his former Freaks and Geeks costar and Dawson’s Creek actress Busy Philipps after she appeared on his show Undeclared.

Recent findings suggest that “She was like, ‘Hey, now that I’m doing this, you gotta do Dawson’s Creek.’ And I was like, ‘Haha,’” Rogen recalled. “And then, like, six months later, I’m on the set of Dawson’s Creek. I was like, ‘How did this happen?’”.

And according to the Emmy winner, the drama wasn’t just onscreen, as he revealed there was plenty behind-the-scenes, too.

It has been revealed that “It was so weird,” he shared. “And there was a lot of resentment between, like, the showrunners and the cast—it was a very bad dynamic.”.

He had quite a harrowing experience away from the set, too, adding, “I was staying in, like, a haunted hotel and had a nervous breakdown.”.

E! News has reached out to Dawson’s Creek creator Kevin Williamson, as well as showrunners Greg Berlanti and Tom Kapinos for comment but has not heard back.

Kapinos previously expressed his own frustration with the series that ran from 1998 to 2003 and starred the late James Van Der Beek, Katie Holmes, Joshua Jackson and Michelle Williams.

"The experience was miserable," he shared during a 2009 Emmys panel. "But it was a four-year boot camp. It was like going to TV grad school and learning how to run a television show. Anybody on that show who could make a decision was allowed to run it at some point. I inherited the very awkward college years, and I almost ran the show into the ground. But I learned everything that I needed to know about how to run a show.".

Still, he was far from the only resident of the Creek who had complications during the series, as Williams explained being on the show for so long deterred her from doing television for a number of years as she feared a “loss of input.”.

As Williams explained, being on the show for so long deterred her from doing television for a number of years as she feared a “loss of input.”.

Recent findings suggest that “Doing Dawson’s Creek for six-and-a-half years, while it was an incredible learning experience—we did 22 episodes a year, and you’d be getting scripts at the last minute and you had zero input,” she shared with actress Patricia Clarkson during an interview for Variety in 2019. “It was a little like a factory job. It was formulaic.”.

For more secrets from the set of Dawson’s Creek, keep reading.

While Fox was first to pick up Dawson's Creek, it subsequently dumped the teen drama.

"I was told they were struggling with Party of Five and they didn't need another one," series creator Kevin Williamson remarked at the 2015 ATX TV Festival.

But that paved the way for The WB to pick it up two years later.

While Paula Cole's "I Don't Want to Wait" became the iconic Dawson's Creek theme song, producers originally wanted Alanis Morissette's "Hand in My Pocket.".

Alas, they couldn't land the rights, what a jagged little pill.

Dawson. Pacey. Joey. Not names you hear every day. So how did Williamson come up with them?

"Dawson came from a real place called Dawson's Creek where we all hung out as kids and partied," he told The Hollywood Reporter in 2018, while Pacey "came from a friend of a friend named Pacey and I'd never met anyone with that name and thought it was a cool name.".

And for the show's heroine, Williamson "wanted Josephine as a very girly name that could easily turn into a tomboy name like Joey.".

Remember Dawson's infamous "walk the dog" line in the pilot?

Williamson inserted the euphemism because the network would not let them say the word "masturbate" in 1998.

Before Katie Holmes was cast in the role that would make her America's sweetheart-next-door, Blair was this close to landing the role.

Industry observers note that "Joe was written to be a tomboy and everyone was coming in being very much a tomboy. We were very close to going with Selma Blair, who was amazing," Williamson told THR. "She read it very tough, with a lot of heart.".

However, once he saw Holmes on tape, with "those two big eyes," Williamson knew they had their Joey.

Joshua Jackson Was Almost Dawson.

Williamson liked Joshua Jackson so much, he didn't care what role the Mighty Ducks alum played.

Industry observers note that "I fell in love with Josh Jackson because he could read any role, Dawson or Pacey," he told THR. "But something wasn't complete and that's when the network mentioned they didn't see Josh as Dawson, and rightfully so. So, I went, 'OK, he's Pacey,' because I knew I wanted him in the show no matter what.".

Charlie Hunnam Auditioned, Won Role of Husband.

An 18-year-old Charlie Hunnam read for the WB drama in 1999 and, while he didn't land the part, he did meet Katherine Towne at his audition.

They tied the knot in Las Vegas three weeks later and divorced in 2002, "three terrible, painful, expensive years later," as Hunnam put it to the Associated Press in 2017.

Dawson's Creek became so popular that American Eagle inked a deal in 2000 to outfit the actors.

The characters wore mostly AE clothes throughout season three, and the cast appeared in ad campaigns and promos for the clothing line, helping drive the company's net income above $105 million in 2001.

When James Van Der Beek was first cast, the studio wanted him to change his hair.

It has been revealed that "We found an ad for The Devil's Own, the movie with Brad Pitt," he recalled to The Daily Beast in 2012. "They said: 'What about Brad Pitt's haircut?' That's how I got my season one haircut.".

Joey and Pacey's Real-Life Love.

Holmes dated Jackson early in the show's run, before Pacey and Joey realized they opposite-of-hated each other.

Industry observers note that "I'm just going to say that I met somebody last year," Holmes told Rolling Stone in 1998, not denying that the somebody was Jackson. "I fell in love, I had my first love, and it was something so incredible and indescribable that I will treasure it always. And that I feel so fortunate because he's now one of my best friends. It's weird, it's almost like a Dawson-and-Joey type thing now.".

It has been revealed that plus one more nugget: "He's been in the business so long," she added, "and he's really helped me. I respect him as a friend and a professional.".

Kerr Smith Didn't Know Jack Was Gay.

When Kerr Smith first signed on to join the show as Joey's upcoming boyfriend, he had no idea the character would eventually come out and be part of the first-ever gay kiss on TV.

Recent findings suggest that "I always knew I wanted Jack to come out of the closet, but I didn't even tell [Smith]," Williamson noted at the ATX TV Festival. "Let the audience love him, then let's have him come out of the closet and have Joey have to deal with that—and then that would eventually drive her back to [Dawson].".

More poignantly, Williamson has mentioned that every character on the show inherited traits from him, including Jack.

Recent findings suggest that “Every single character has a trait of me in them,” he told Entertainment Weekly in 2018. “I had just, in my 20s, gone through the coming-out process and had told my parents I was gay. I had taken that whole journey, and I wanted a character on the show to represent that journey and to represent that side of me.".

Jack's coming out episode, cowritten by Williamson and producer Greg Berlanti, was inspired by true events.

"A friend of mine had a story that I brought in that he got outed accidentally," Berlanti told EW, "because he wrote a love poem that it was so clear to everyone else that it was about a guy.”.

Michelle Williams and Busy Philipps' best-friendship, which first blossomed on Dawson's Creek, is still going strong to this day.

“I’m so in love with her,” Williams told People of her bestie at a 2016 screening of Manchester by the Sea, one of many red carpet date nights for the besties. “She’s proof that the love of your life does not have to be a man! That’s the love of my life right there.”.

Philipps is also godmother to Williams' daughter Matilda Ledger, who was born in 2005.

Dawson finally losing his virginity was such a major show moment that Van Der Beek brought a very special gift to set the day the scene was filmed.

"I remember bringing champagne for the crew—Dawson finally lost his virginity!" he told The Daily Beast.

Chad Michael Murray, One Tree Heel?

Before starring on One Tree Hill, Chad Michael Murray had an arc on Dawson's Creek playing Charlie, a love interest for Jen and Joey.

But while Charlie got around, Murray didn't seem to make a lot of friends during his first stint in North Carolinav (OTH later filmed there).

During a Paley panel in 2009, Philipps called him "a douche," later saying, "Don't worry. I'm not real worried about burning bridges with CMM.".

Van Der Beek added, "He's actually come a long way." Post-event, Philipps tweeted, "Just finished the dawson's creek panel. Maybe I was too harsh on chadM2… Nah.".

Murray, meanwhile, hasn't stirred the pot, saying in 2015 that he learned a lot from the experience.

“I had the opportunity to learn from people who had been doing it for a couple of years longer than I was when I walked into the Dawson’s cast,” he told Cosmpolitan.com in 2015. “You know, Michelle and James and Katie and Josh—they really kind of guided me, because they’d already been around for five, six years, maybe longer. And if they had the time, they were showing me the ropes. I had no idea what lighting was, I had no idea about a lot of the technical aspects of what we do, and so I’m grateful for that experience.”.

Just a sampling of the famous faces, ranging from the already familiar to future huge stars, who appeared on Dawson's Creek over the years: Seth Rogen, Jane Lynch, Julie Bowen, Scott Foley, Jensen Ackles, Hilarie Burton, Rachel Leigh Cook, Ali Larter and Oliver Hudson.

Young Americans was a short-lived spinoff centering on Pacey's friend Will Krudski (Rodney Scott) and his boarding school classmates at Rawley Academy.

Also starring Ian Somerhalder and Kate Bosworth, it was canceled after just one season.

The Show Almost Ended With Joey Picking Dawson.

The show's main love triangle officially disassembled when Joey chose Pacey in the 2003 series finale.

But it almost didn't turn out that way, as Williamson first envisioned Dawson getting the girl. But halfway through writing the finale, Williamson realized that a happy ending for that couple wasn't "what the show was set to be.".

Recent findings suggest that "I wanted it to be a twist on the teen genre but also wanted it to be surprising, honest and real and say something about soul mates and what soul mates can be," he explained at the ATX TV Festival. "That's why we did it that way. When you left the show in that last moment, they're a family and everyone got what they wanted. There was fulfillment and they were all happy.".

At the last minute, he changed his mind and the rest is TV history. But Williamson admitted his mom, who played for Team Dawson, was not happy.

In the finale, which jumped ahead five years, the group had to deal with the devastating loss of Jen.

It has been revealed that "Dealing with the death of one of their own was the final thing that thrust them into adulthood forever. Dawson's Creek was a coming-of-age story and that was the idea behind that ending," Williamson explained of the decision. "That's why we killed Jen, because I wanted them to deal with a death of one their own as that final lesson.".

Some of the executive producers who get their start on Dawson's?

Julie Plec (who went on to gift us with The Vampire Diaries and The Originals), Berlanti (Everwood, Arrow, The Flash, Riverdale...the list goes on and on, and that doesn't even include his movies), Rob Thomas (Veronica Mars and iZombie), Jenny Bicks (Sex and the City), Anna Fricke (Being Human), Dana Baratta (Jessica Jones) and many more.

Senegal have been reinstated as the champions of Africa, and their controversial 1-0 victory against Morocco confirmed in the record books, after the scandal over January’s Africa Cup of Nations final was resolved in a Swiss courtroom.

It has been revealed that the court of arbitration for sport (Cas) ruled that a decision to award the 2025 Afcon title to Morocco on appeal should be set aside. Senegal celebrated with a social media post proclaiming the team to have won the title twice: first on the field and then at Cas. Morocco, who are due to co-host the World Cup in 2030, declared their intention to “pursue all legal avenues” to challenge the ruling.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia has reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO less than two weeks after he stepped down, and less than a week after the firm's board remarked it had no intention of bringing him back.
  • According to recent reports, nvidia announced Huang's resignation on Nov.
  • While Huang said that he would be "honored" to return as CEO if asked, the board said on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia has reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO less than two weeks after he stepped down, and less than a week after the firm's board remarked it had no intention of bringing him back. Reactions to Huang's return have been a mix of praise, criticism, and jokes, with several other tech executives rallying around him.

According to recent reports, nvidia announced Huang's resignation on Nov. 12, a day after the board accepted it with immediate effect. He stepped down amid reports that he'd had extramarital affairs with both an alleged Chinese spy and a Nvidia employee, with allegations of a third affair with another worker subsequently surfacing. His relationship with Alice Huang (no relation) drew particular scrutiny, as she was suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips. She previously worked as an executive at Megaspeed, a organization U.S. authorities have been investigating over concerns it smuggled advanced Nvidia chips to China in circumvention of U.S. restrictions.

While Huang said that he would be "honored" to return as CEO if asked, the board said on Nov. 17 that it did not plan to bring him back. Yet after reported pressure from President Donald Trump, the chipmaker has put Huang back in the top job after all. In a press release announcing Huang's reinstatement, Nvidia stated that it had based the decision on "input from senior levels of the United States government.".

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," said Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones, who last week said that the organization "does not intend to reinstate Jensen.".

In a recent development, trump has been characteristically celebratory about Nvidia's decision, making several posts on his social media platform Truth Social on the topic. This included an edited image based on a photo of Trump after a shooter attempted to assassinate him in 2024. Originally posted by X account @grandoldmemes, the picture has been edited to show Huang holding a red bra aloft as a Nvidia banner is displayed in the background.

Calling Huang's reinstatement an "absolutely GREAT decision" (emphasis original), Trump stated that having him installed as Nvidia's CEO is vital to the U.S. economy.

"The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at Nvidia in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy," wrote Trump. "The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security…. On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure.".

The U.S. president also spoke about Huang's reinstatement in a phone call to CNBC on Monday.

"I think he's gonna start off at an almost higher level," Trump remarked. "He's apologised for [his] indiscretion, which was unfortunate. Probably that’s what brought it to such a level, because sex sells, fellas. Now [CNBC host Jim] Cramer would not know that because he’s a very, very, very committed person. But sex sells.".

Trump's on-and-off ally Elon Musk also celebrated Huang's return, reposting Nvidia's announcement on X and writing that "the mistake has been corrected." Last week, Musk stated that he was signing a petition to reinstate Nvidia's then-ousted CEO.

Industry observers note that "Everyone I know at Nvidia wanted Jensen back and it shows," the Tesla and SpaceX CEO continued, sharing a post from investor Gavin Baker. In it, Baker shared images of people crowding around Huang and applauding him on his return to Nvidia's offices.

It has been revealed that "Grateful to the President, everyone in the administration, everyone who signed the petition, everyone who supported Jensen publicly, everyone who called the board, everyone on the board who fought for him, everyone," Baker wrote. "This is why America is the greatest country on earth." The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile Products available for purchase through affiliate links. In a recent development, musk himself was ousted as CEO of X.com in 2000 after it merged with Confinity, the company behind PayPal. He had reportedly wanted to phase out the PayPal name in favor of X.com, despite concerns about its explicit connotations.

Various other prominent figures in tech have also voiced support for Huang's return, several of whom have previously faced comparable turmoil at their own companies.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman appeared to express approval for Huang's reinstatement, publishing a post on X that simply read, "Jensen!" Altman went through a similar incident when OpenAI's board fired him in 2023, accusing him of lying, retaliating against critics, and creating a "toxic atmosphere." Despite these allegations, Altman was ultimately reinstated after days of outcry from supporters.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, Binance co-founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao posted to X that he was "glad to see @JensenHuang back," resharing his previous reaction that it was "a mistake for Nvidia to let Jensen resign." Zhao resigned from his role as CEO of Binance and pleaded guilty to failing to maintain an effective anti-money laundering program in 2023, serving a four-month prison sentence. However, he remains Binance's majority shareholder and retains significant influence over the global cryptocurrency exchange.

Sources indicate that "Jensen is a great man, flawed like the rest of us, but at the same time the best amongst us," Kalanick posted to X on Monday. "The world and humanity needs him to fight for a shot at liberty, a counterweight to techno-authoritarianism.".

Sources indicate that kalanick resigned from his role as Uber CEO in 2017 after demands from multiple major investors. This came after Kalanick took a leave of absence amid allegations of a misogynistic workplace culture. Though one of the investors sued Kalanick for fraud later that year, the ousted CEO remained on Uber's board until resigning in 2019.

Telegram CEO Pavel Durov also celebrated Huang's return, posting "Jensen's back" with a party popper emoji. He then joked about the situation, writing that "Nvidia's board finally accepted that a CEO has to evaluate Chinese models personally. You can't delegate that.".

Durov was ousted from his former role as CEO of Russian social media platform VK in 2014 after the board mentioned it had accepted a resignation he'd submitted and failed to withdraw. Durov claimed the resignation had been an April Fools' joke and suggested that his firing was politically motivated.

Given their own personal experiences, it's no surprise that many former and current tech executives have supported Huang's return as Nvidia's CEO. Other reactions have been a mixed bag — some celebrating the news, some condemning it, and others simply enjoying the jokes and memes.

"Reinstating Huang is a disaster for corporate governance and even the rule of law, but it is objectively very very funny," author and tech reporter David Z. Morris posted to X.

Some have also noted the timing of Huang's temporary ousting, joking that he deliberately orchestrated several days away from work in order to play Grand Theft Auto VI.

It's been a tumultuous few weeks for Nvidia, and it's unclear how the organization plans to move forward at this stage. However, whatever happens, the jokes will likely continue for a while.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that spaceX rolled out a classified mission for the U.S.
  • A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m.
  • The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that spaceX rolled out a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast.

A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317.

The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100.

SpaceX ended its launch webcast just after that touchdown, so we didn't get to see the Falcon 9's upper stage power its way to orbit.

USSF-317 is a classified mission, so we don't know what the upper stage is carrying or where exactly it's headed. However, some experts think that USSF-317 may be hauling a batch of SpaceX's Starshield satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO) for the Space Force's Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, which helps the military keep tabs on potential targets around the world.

NROL-105 | USSF-385 | 8 Starlink missions.

USSF-317 was the 121st Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and the third mission that SpaceX has debuted for the Space Force so far in November.

The vast majority of this year's Falcon 9 missions — about 70% of them — have been devoted to building out SpaceX's Starlink LEO internet constellation, which right now consists of more than 11,000 satellites.

According to recent reports, the Falcon 9 has been putting up incredible numbers lately — it flew a whopping 165 times in 2025, for example — but the workhorse rocket is on its way out. SpaceX aims to retire both it and the Falcon Heavy in favor of its fully reusable Starship megarocket, which deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites on its most recent two test flights.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Brad Pitt is sitting out of this one adventure.

One week after attending the Los Angeles premiere of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth in Los Angeles, the actor unexpectedly skipped the Netflix movie’s red carpet rollout in London due to illness.

Ahead of the Nov. 23 event, its organizers told British outlet The Independent in a statement that Pitt was “is no longer able to attend the premiere as he has come down with flu and has been advised not to travel.".

Amid his sickness, the 62-year-old made the decision to focus on the long-term health of himself and his cast.

Industry observers note that “He has had the flu for a few days and didn’t want to get anyone sick,” a source close to Pitt told E! News. “He is recovering and looking forward to future screenings.”.

Pitt’s costars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller, as well as director David Fincher, still attended the premiere, which was held at the BFI IMAX in the English capital.

While Pitt may not have been present at The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’s latest premiere, the film—a sequel to Quentin Tarantino’s 2019 movie Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood—is missing his onscreen wingman Leonardo DiCaprio entirely after the Titanic alum opted to sit out.

It has been revealed that "It would have been great fun, but it required a lot of prosthetics, which is a good couple of weeks prepping to get him," Pitt told The Hollywood Reporter earlier this month, referring to how the trailer teased that DiCaprio's Rick Dalton character had become "too fat" for his titular stuntman to serve as a body double. "It’s hardly worth the cost for a cameo.".

He added, "It was talked about for a while, but it just seemed like a big ask.”.

And DiCaprio confirmed he wouldn’t reprise his role ahead of the sequel, too.

“There were some talks about it early on,” he told Deadline last year. Still, he added, “Ultimately, I cannot wait to see the Cliff Booth story, but I’m not in it.”.

While Pitt is returning to reprise his Oscar-winning role, read on to learn about the legendary parts he turned down.

Pitt was almost the One. "I did pass on 'The Matrix," the superstar recently admitted at the Santa Barbara International Film Festival in January. "I took the red pill. That's the only one I'm naming…I wasn't offered two or three. Only the first one, just to clarify that.".

As we all know, Keanu Reeves went on to be Neo, and is presently filming the fourth film in the franchise, though producer Lorenzeo di Bonaventura once revealed Will Smith, Leonardo DiCaprio and Sandra Bullock were all in consideration in addition to Pitt.

Recent findings suggest that while it's hard to imagine anyone but Billy Crudup as Russell Hammond in Cameron Crowe's 2000 classic Almost Famous, Pitt was originally set to play the complicated rocker. But, according to the writer and director, who wrote the part with the star in mind, Pitt worked with Crowe for months before ultimately leaving the project, making way for Crudup to have his breakthrough performance.

"His head was still in Fight Club and the part was a little underwritten. It was the most underwritten in the script, and he couldn't trust it enough," Crowe told AL.com in 2014. "I've talked to him since. I love the guy. I think he's hilarious, and I thought he would have been funny in the movie. If I had waited a few more months, he might have come around to it, but we had to get going. But Billy Crudup worked out great.".

Recent findings suggest that while it's widely considered one of the best films of all-time, Pitt infamously pulled out of the movie, with Gil Bellows ultimately taking over the small but pivotal role of prisoner Tommy. "These are the adventures in castings," director Frank Darabont told USA Today. "But it would be really fun to bump into Brad Pitt and say, 'Weren't you that guy?' I'd love to give him a little (grief) about that just for fun.".

According to recent reports, after just landing his breakout role in Thelma & Louise, he ultimately decided to star in Interview With the Vampire over Shawshank. And he told the publication he had no regrets. "It would have been kind of cool to be in, but I'm not a regret guy in that way," he explained. "I just believe in the way things work out, and that was someone else's role. Even the feeling of, 'Ooh, that would've been nice' would redirect a choice later down the road. So it all works in tandem in that way.".

After working together on Ocean's 11, Matt Damon ended up snagging the lead role as spy Jason Bourne in The Bourne Identity when Pitt became unavailable, ironically, due to his commitment to Spy Game. After he reportedly passed, Damon received the offer that would result in a major movie franchise that has grossed over $1.6 billion worldwide.

Did you know Pitt and Leonardo DiCaprio almost worked together years before finally collaborating on Once Upon a Time…in Hollywood? Pitt had originally bought the rights to remake the Hong Kong hit Internal Affairs, which ultimately became The Departed, with him slated to play Sullivan. But when the star dropped out, saying a younger actor should play the part—"I thought I was too old for it," he told Interview—Matt Damon once again filled in, with Pitt remaining a producer on the film.

While Christian Bale ultimately took on the murderous role of Patrick Batemen, turning in one of his most memorable performances, an earlier version of the film was set to star Pitt and be directed by David Cronenberg before creative differences halted the project.

"Yes, in the early Nineties with a young actor attached named Brad Pitt. David was lovely—is lovely, I still like David—but he had strange demands. He hated shooting restaurant scenes, and he hated shooting nightclub scenes," writer Bret Easton Ellis revealed to Rolling Stone. "And he didn't want to shoot the violence. I ignored everything he stated. So of course he was disappointed with it and he hired his own writer; that script was worse for him and he dropped out.".

While he never technically auditioned for the part, there is a tape out there of Pitt reading the iconic role of J.D., which ultimately went to Christian Slater, at a table-read of Heathers ahead of its 1988 release.

"We just gathered actors that we knew and friends that we had to read the roles. And an actress named Stacey Travis—who was a friend of ours—was in an acting class and we didn't have anybody to read the part of J.D," director Michael Lehmann explained to Fandom. "So we asked Stacey and she brought this young kid from her class. A good looking kid, he cold-read part of J.D. in the table-read, and years later I found out if was Brad Pitt.".

An ancient virus may help explain what makes the human brain different

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (955 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A virus that infected chimpanzees millions of years ago has left behind a genetic legacy that may help explain an important difference between human and chimpanzee brain development.
  • It has been revealed that the findings, published in Science Advances, reveal how infections from the distant past can leave lasting changes in the genetic makeup of an entire population.
  • Industry observers note that although pandemics are often considered a modern threat, infectious diseases have been spreading through large animal and human populations for millions of years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A virus that infected chimpanzees millions of years ago has left behind a genetic legacy that may help explain an important difference between human and chimpanzee brain development. Researchers at Lund University have discovered that ancient viral DNA embedded in the chimpanzee genome switches off a gene that remains active in humans and appears to play an important role in the developing brain.

It has been revealed that the findings, published in Science Advances, reveal how infections from the distant past can leave lasting changes in the genetic makeup of an entire population. They also offer new clues about how the brains of humans and our closest evolutionary relatives may have developed differently.

Industry observers note that although pandemics are often considered a modern threat, infectious diseases have been spreading through large animal and human populations for millions of years. Some of these ancient infections left traces of viral DNA that continue to influence how genes function today.

Johan Jakobsson, Professor of Molecular Neurogenetics at Lund University, says the discovery demonstrates how a virus can introduce genetic changes that eventually become widespread throughout a population.

In a recent development, "The virus we investigated specifically affected chimpanzees. Yet humans and chimpanzees have largely the same genetic makeup. That is why it is important to understand the differences in how genes are regulated. Our findings suggest that one gene, LINC00662, plays a significant role in early human brain development," indicates Johan Jakobsson.

How an Ancient Virus Silenced a Brain Development Gene.

At the center of the discovery is a gene called LINC00662. Researchers found that it is active during early human brain development but completely switched off in comparable chimpanzee brain models.

The difference appears to be caused by a genetic remnant of PTERV1, an ancient virus that infected chimpanzees millions of years ago. PTERV1 belongs to a group known as endogenous retroviruses, which are viruses whose genetic material became incorporated into the DNA of their hosts. Once embedded in the genome, these viral sequences can be inherited by future generations.

Over time, PTERV1 produced numerous copies of its genetic material that became scattered across different parts of the chimpanzee genome. Researchers found that these viral sequences are systematically silenced through a process called methylation.

It has been revealed that methylation involves chemical modifications to DNA that help regulate gene activity. It is one of the ways cells control which genetic instructions are used and which remain inactive. In this case, the ancient viral insertion appears to have caused a neighboring gene involved in brain development to be switched off.

Jakobsson says understanding these differences in gene regulation could also provide key insights into how genetic activity protects the brain or contributes to damage and disease.

Miniature Brains Reveal a Striking Genetic Difference.

To investigate the virus's effects, researchers grew miniature brain models called organoids using stem cells from humans and chimpanzees. These three-dimensional structures reproduce certain features of developing brain tissue, allowing scientists to study aspects of early brain development under controlled laboratory conditions.

When the team compared the two types of organoids, the difference was striking. LINC00662 revealed strong activity in the human brain models but was completely inactive in those derived from chimpanzee cells.

"The gene was strongly expressed in the human organoids, but not at all in the chimpanzee organoids," notes Patricia Gerdes, postdoc in molecular neurogenetics at Lund University.

The researchers then set out to determine whether the ancient viral DNA was directly responsible for this difference.

Using CRISPR-Cas9, a powerful gene editing technology that allows scientists to make targeted changes to DNA, they removed the viral sequence from chimpanzee cells.

The result provided compelling evidence. Once the viral DNA was removed, the previously inactive LINC00662 gene switched back on.

"This shows that it is in fact the viral insertion that is responsible for the gene being switched off in chimpanzees," notes Patricia Gerdes.

New Clues to Human Brain Evolution.

In a recent development, the team also wanted to understand what LINC00662 actually does in the human brain. To investigate, they used CRISPR to switch off the gene in human brain organoids and examined how other genes responded.

Disabling LINC00662 reduced the activity of genes associated with nerve cell development and the formation of connections between neurons. These processes are essential for establishing the networks that allow the brain to communicate and function.

The results suggest that LINC00662 contributes to important stages of early human brain development, while the ancient viral insertion prevents the gene from functioning in chimpanzees.

More broadly, the discovery highlights an crucial principle of evolution. Although humans and chimpanzees share much of their genetic material, differences in how genes are switched on and off can influence how their bodies and brains develop.

The findings suggest that ancient viral infections may have contributed to these differences by altering gene regulation long after the original infections disappeared.

Researchers now plan to investigate whether other remnants of ancient viruses have similarly influenced brain evolution. They also hope to determine whether these inherited viral sequences may play a role in neurological diseases.

Together, the discoveries raise an intriguing possibility that some of the differences between human and chimpanzee brains may trace back, at least in part, to viruses that infected our evolutionary relatives millions of years ago.

Materials provided by Lund University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

Mabel Willis turned 11 on Sunday, and her proud mom marked the occasion by sharing a montage of family photos and videos taken over the years, set to the song “Pictures Of You” by The Cure.

“Happy 11th Birthday Mabel Ray!” Heming Willis wrote in the caption.

Emma Heming Willis speaks out about finding community as a caregiver: 'This journey can feel very dark'.

“Your energy is infectious,” she continued, praising her little girl for the way she “can light a whole room with your smile and warmth.”.

Industry observers note that willis is clearly a doting dad. One picture in Heming Willis’ montage indicates the “Die Hard” star holding baby Mabel while planting a kiss on her forehead, while a more recent image shows a beaming Willis hanging out in nature with his preteen.

Bruce Willis sings with his family in birthday tribute video from ex Demi Moore.

Heming Willis penned an equally heartfelt tribute last month when her husband celebrated his 68th birthday. Sharing a video montage on Instagram, she referred to the actor as “pure love.”.

In February, Willis’ family revealed that his speaking disorder, aphasia, had progressed into a form of dementia called frontotemporal dementia, or FTD.

It has been revealed that “Today there are no treatments for the disease, a reality that we hope can change in the years ahead,” they noted in an revision shared online. “As Bruce’s condition advances, we hope that any media attention can be focused on shining a light on this disease that needs far more awareness and research.”.

According to the Alzheimer’s Association, FTD refers to “a group of disorders caused by progressive nerve cell loss in the brain’s frontal lobes (the areas behind your forehead) or its temporal lobes.” These areas of the brain are generally associated with personality, behavior and language.

Gabriel Iglesias experienced a health scare onstage.

The comedian abruptly sought treatment from backstage medics during his Nov. 22 show at the Lenovo Center in Raleigh, N.C., as seen in social media footage shared from the performance.

In the video posted by an audience member to TikTok shortly after the show, Iglesias was in the middle of his routine when he keeled over a stool beside his microphone stand, seemingly using the seat to support himself up. The 50-year-old was then escorted backstage, where he appeared to use an oxygen mask as medical workers surrounded him. In the background, an announcer told the crowd that the show was over.

According to recent reports, while Iglesias did not disclose what caused him to stop the performance, his rep told E! News in a Nov. 23 statement he is “doing much better today” after being “sick the last week or so.”.

“He didn’t want to cancel on his fans,” his rep added, “so he tried to pull through to give them a great show.”.

The North Carolina show was just the latest stop in Iglesias’ ongoing 1976 Tour: A Fluffy Celebration, which gets its name from the year he was born, as well as his nickname “Fluffy.”.

Through the years, the Ferdinand actor has been candid about his health struggles, sharing in his 2014 documentary The Fluffy Movie that he was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and was originally given two years to live.

"That's the biggest wake-up call you can get,” he told Buzzfeed in 2015. “Your habit is hurting you. You need to check yourself. You still have a chance.".

The diagnosis made him reprioritize his health, sharing that he started making an effort to go to the gym more regularly and make changes in his diet.

Industry observers note that "It has nothing to do with the way I look," he explained. "The amount of attention that I get as a significant dude is amazing. I'm trying to improve my [health] so I can be around.”.

For more stars who have experienced their own health scares, keep reading.

Travis Barker's Precancer Diagnosis.

The Blink-182 drummer stopped smoking weed after being diagnosed with "precancer of the esophagus.".

"I loved blunts and I would smoke too much," he shared on a November 2026 episode of the Big Bro with Kid Cudi podcast, recalling how his doctor stated it was a "serious case. "He’s like, ‘This is your warning shot. Don’t f--l around. You’ve got to stop smoking.".

While Ryan described her first four concussions as "incidents," she noted her fifth one was trauma caused by "sustained shaking over a minute of time.".

Now, the former Disney Channel star needs to close her eyes to "think better.".

"Quite often the world is really loud. It’s really too bright. There’s a lot going on," she explained. "The visual data that I'm taking in can be so distracting and so loud. Then, with the migraines—which are significantly worsened by that—it sort of is too much.".

According to recent reports, "It's OK," she told sister Bella Garcia at the time. "We're going to get it fixed one day. I told the doctor, I go, 'Newly divorced, so the minute the boots are hung up, I'm going to come back to you and we're going to make these girls look real good, because these girls are going to get some action in the future and that can't look like that.'".

In October 2026, the former The Bachelorette star detailed how she cracked a vertebra in her spine after setting her vibration plate—a motorized platform that rapidly moves back and forth to promote muscle activation and circulation—to "level 30, supersonic speed.".

"Seemingly, subtly, somewhere on the way to 30, maybe 10 or 20, my vertebrae turn crooked and rub against each other," Windey shared in a Substack essaye aptly titled "Broke back, no mountain.".

In a recent development, "It was too fast vibrations I guess, and too many vibrations maybe, and too much pressure to shake," she continued. "And it broke. Broke right off, like your ex-boyfriend’s bumper. Well, technically, it cracked.".

The injury left her with what she described as "insatiable" paresthesia—a medical term for a tingling, pins-and-needles sensation.

According to recent reports, "This is the greatest sense of condemnation; of persecution, I’ll ever feel," she added. "And I do wish it on my worst enemy If only they hadn’t wished it on me first.".

Lupita Nyong'o's Uterine Fibroids.

The 12 Years a Slave star was diagnosed with uterine fibroids—non-cancerous growths that develop in or around the uterus—in 2014, the same year she won an Oscar for performance in the movie.

However, it wasn't until 2025 when she disclosed her diagnosis, writing on Instagram that she had been "suffering in silence" for more than a decade.

"When we reach puberty, we're taught periods mean pain, and that pain is simply part of being a woman," she shared. "We're struggling alone with something that affects us most.".

Brian Austin Green's Perforated Appendix.

The Beverly Hills, 90210 alum revealed in April 2025 that he was recovering from surgery after his appendix nearly burst.

“Last week, I started feeling some pain in my stomach,” Brian noted in an Instagram video at the time. “I ended up going to the emergency room, and I had a perforated appendix. Not quite burst, but just before.”.

He added, “I'm on the road to recovery. It's not an easy process. This is my first major surgery.”.

In July 2025, the Daisy Jones & The Six star shared that she had been hospitalized due to a hernia—a gap in the muscular wall that's commonly found in the abdomen or groin area—caused by wearing tight pants.

"'Suki you never tweet anymore,'" she wrote on X, formerly known as Twitter. "Have you ever considered I wore pants so tight 6 months ago it caused a hernia & I’ve been too scared to tell you?".

Savannah DeMelo's Mid-Game "Medical Emergency" Mid-Game.

The Racing Louisville midfielder collapsed just a few minutes into her soccer team's September 2025 match against Seattle Reign at Lumen Field in Seatle.

The United States Women’s National Team player could be seen slowly sitting down on the field with a teammate by her side, per Reuters, as the referee called for trainers to check her out. She collapsed seconds later.

“Savannah received immediate on-field care from medical personnel and was transported to a local hospital for further evaluation,” the National Women’s Soccer League wrote on X later that night. “She is stable and alert.".

Adam Devine's Long-Term Injury From Childhood Accident.

Adam Devine shared that injuries he sustained after getting hit by a cement truck when he was 11 years old are still affecting him to this day.

It has been revealed that “It’s been a nightmare,” Devine noted in a 2025 episode of the In Depth With Graham Bensinger podcast. “I have spasms all over. For a while, [the doctors] told me I was dying—literally, within this last year.”.

He noted that pain comes and goes, adding, "My body has all these things that are a little wonky and a little wrong with it.".

The Bachelor Nation alum shared that he went to the hospital “crawling on all fours” due to overwhelming back pain that was aggravated during an RV trip with a friend.

“Right now, knees to my toes, it’s, like, still tingly, which is crazy,” he mentioned on a March 2025 episode of his Trading Secrets podcast. “And to put in perspective, I don’t know, man, like not to sound douchey, but like two, three weeks ago, maybe a month ago, I was squatting probably like 295 pounds. And right now, I can’t do a squat on my foot. I can’t do a one legged squat, I fall. It’s like I had a stroke or something.”.

But with the help of a back specialist and some steroids, he added, “We’re on the mend.”.

Matt Kirschenheiter's Heart Attack.

Real Housewives of Orange County’s Gina Kirschenheiter shared her ex-husband Matt Kirschenheiter suffered a heart attack in March 2025, but thankfully survived the ordeal.

Tracy Morgan's Medical Emergency.

The 30 Rock star suffered a health scare at a Latest York Knicks basketball game in March 2025, leading to him being wheeled out of Madison Square Garden.

However, the comedian shared an enhancement on social media the following day, noting it was a case of food poisoning and that he was on the mend.

Christy Carlson Romano's Eye Injury.

The Even Stevens alum shared in February 2025 that she was shot in the face while on a trip to shoot clay pigeons to celebrate husband Brendan Rooney's birthday.

According to recent reports, "There was another party with us and they unsafely fired in the wrong direction and shot me in the face," she wrote on Instagram. "@thebrendanrooney immediately sprung into action, assessed me, and rushed me to the hospital. I was hit in 5 places, one was less than an inch from hitting me directly in my right eye.".

It has been revealed that the Kim Possible alum continued, "Unfortunately a fragment got lodged behind my eye and it is too risky to remove surgically at this time. Doctors will continue to monitor me (I can see normally at the moment).".

Recent findings suggest that the actress mentioned she was grateful to be alive. "I love my daughters, husband, family, and friends so much," she said. "I saw my life flash before my eyes and I’m telling you, hug the people around you every chance you can. Life can change in an instant.".

While the internet isn't always a kind place, Amy Schumer is happy that, in this case, it helped her get answers."The internet really came for me after doing a bunch of press, and I was like, 'OK everybody, relax,'" Amy recalled of her "puffier" face on a January 2025 episode of Call Her Daddy. "But then doctors were chiming in in the comments and they were like, 'No no, we think something’s really up. Your face looks so crazy that we think something’s up. And I’m like, ‘Wait, I’m getting trolled by doctors?’"After these doctors said they thought she had Cushing syndrome and that it may be caused by spiking coritsol levels or steroid injections, the Life & Beth creator thought, "Wait, I have been getting steroid injections in my scars.""I had a breast reduction, a C-section, whatever, and so I was getting these steroid injections," Amy said. "So it gave me this thing called Cushing syndrome, which I wouldn’t have known if the internet hadn’t come for me so hard."Toda, Amy is just relieved she's OK. As she shared in a February 2024 News Not Noise newsletter, "Finding out I have the kind of Cushing that will just work itself out and I'm healthy was the greatest news imaginable.".

Casey Fitzgerald's Neck Injury From Hockey Skate Blade.

The AHL player was cut by a fellow player's skate during a game in December 2024 and received 25 stitches. His father, Fresh Jersey Devils general manager Tom Fitzgerald later told ESPN after his son was fully recovered, "We're very lucky. I don't wish that on any parent.".

Hailey Bieber had the "scariest moment" of her life when she was having breakfast with husband Justin Bieber and started experiencing stroke-like symptoms in March 2022."Justin was like, 'Are you OK?'" the Rhode skincare mogul shared a month later on YouTube, "and I just didn't respond because I wasn't sure. And then he asked me again and when I went to respond, I couldn't speak. The right side of my face started drooping. I couldn't get a sentence out."While Hailey stated the facial drooping stopped and her speech came back, she went to the hospital to make sure she was OK."They did some scans and they were able to see that I had suffered a small blood clot to my brain," the model added, "which they labeled and categorized as something called a TIA [Transient Ischemic Attack]."Later, Hailey went to the University of California, Los Angeles, where she found out she had a hole in her heart called a patent foramen ovale (PFO).She explained the blood clot had traveled into her heart, "escaped" through the hole and went to her brain, leading to the TIA.Hailey said she had a successful PFO closure procedure and was now feeling great.

Justin Bieber's Ramsay Hunt Syndrome.

"As you can see, this eye is not blinking. I can't smile on this side of my face. This nostril will not move. So, there's full paralysis on this side of my face."In fact, he told his followers it had gotten "progressively harder to eat." But after a while, the paralysis went away."He's doing really well," Hailey mentioned on a June 2022 episode of Good Morning America, later adding, "He's feeling a lot better. Obviously, it was just a very scary and random situation to happen, but he's going to be totally OK and I'm just grateful that he's fine.".

Jamie Foxx's Brain Bleed & Stroke.

While Jamie Foxx initially kept details of his April 2023 hospitalization private, he later opened up about what he went through.One day in Atlanta, "I was having such a bad headache, so I asked my boy, I said, ‘Listen, I need an aspirin,’” the Oscar winner said in his 2024 Netflix special What Had Happened Was... “Before I could get the Aspirin, I went out. I don’t remember 20 days.”Jamie said he was initially taken to a doctor who gave him a cortisone shot and then sent him home. However, his concerned sister Deidra Dixon then drove him to a hospital, where they got an answer: He had a brain bleed that led to a stroke.Twenty days after undergoing an operation, the Django Unchained woke up May 4 in a wheelchair and couldn’t walk. He then went to Chicago for rehabilitation and therapy."All I can tell you is that I appreciate every prayer,” he said, “because I needed every prayer.”.

Tracey Yukich's Medical Emergency on The Biggest Loser.

The reality star revealed that she "died" while running a mile during the first challenge of the NBC competition series.

“I don't remember a lot,” she explained on Fit for TV: The Reality of The Biggest Loser. “I remember hearing the helicopter. I just felt like I was floating. And then my grandpa was there. And then I saw darkness. But then I saw light. So I knew, I knew I died that day.”.

“My organs were literally shutting down,” she continued. “I didn't realize that I had rhabdomyolysis. And rhabdomyolysis is your body's way of saying, ‘I'm going to shut down on you.’”.

According to recent reports, emilia Clarke filmed battle scenes for Game of Thrones, but in 2019, she published an essay in The New Yorker titled "A Battle for My Life."Having a bad headache at the gym, "I reached the toilet, sank to my knees, and proceeded to be violently, voluminously ill," the actress wrote. "Meanwhile, the pain—shooting, stabbing, constricting pain—was getting worse. At some level, I knew what was happening: my brain was damaged."She was taken to the hospital for a brain scan."The diagnosis was quick and ominous: a subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), a life-threatening type of stroke, caused by bleeding into the space surrounding the brain," the Emmy nominee added. "I’d had an aneurysm, an arterial rupture."Emilia had immediate surgery to seal the aneurysm, calling the pain "unbearable." While she was recovering, she continued, she experienced aphasia and was "muttering nonsense."A week later, "the aphasia passed," Emilia added, and she left the hospital a month after being admitted. At a 2013 brain scan, she learned a growth "doubled in size" and that she needed surgery again."When they woke me, I was screaming in pain," she wrote. "The procedure had failed. I had a massive bleed and the doctors made it plain that my chances of surviving were precarious if they didn’t operate again. This time they needed to access my brain in the old-fashioned way—through my skull."Thankfully, Emilia shared, she's now "at a hundred per cent.".

Snoop Dogg's daughter Cori Broadus is grateful for her family.Because after she suffered a "severe stroke" in January 2024, her loved ones rushed to be by her side."I texted them that I just had a stroke and sent them a picture," she told E! News correspondent Will Marfuggi in December 2024. "Everybody just came to my rescue."Because of other medical concerns, Cori ended up staying in the hospital longer than she initially expected."I could have went home after my stroke, but my lupus wasn't doing so well," the Snoop's Fatherhood: Cori and Wayne's Story star continued. "My kidneys were failing. It was a lot going on."Today, Cori is on the mend."I'm doing great," she added. "I just had a little bit of motor skills that I had to work back on. But other than that, I was fine.".

Shailene Woodley's Health Battle.

Shailene Woodley’s early 20s were not an easy time health-wise.“It got to the point where I was losing my hearing. I couldn’t walk for longer than five minutes at a time without having to lay down for hours, and hours and sleep. Everything I ate hurt my stomach,” the actress mentioned on a September 2024 episode of the SHE MD Podcast. “It was this conflation of concerns and diagnoses and different doctors telling me different things.”So Shailene—who chose to keep the exact condition private—set out to find answers. “I come from a very holistic background and study herbalism,” she added. “So I was very keen on, ‘I’m going to work with real MDs, [and] I’m also going to work with independent kind of healers.’ Just trying to search for some sense of comfort in my own skin.”It was a long journey—one that lasted for 10 years.“Throughout that decade, a lot of other things came from feeling so much discomfort physically,” the Massive Little Lies star noted, “which was, ‘My gosh, if everything I eat hurts my stomach, I’m now suddenly afraid of food.’ And then going into the kind of mental f--ckery that can happen with that of body dysmorphia and confusion about identity and feeling safe in my own capsule, in my own skin, what that meant, and what that should be.”After tending to both her physical and mental health, Shailene is feeling much better.“It was a journey that ultimately physically resolved itself, and I am very healthy,” she shared. “I’m so happy to be able to say that.".

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three astronauts will launch aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft.Credit: Xinhua/Shutterstock.

For the first time, China will send a foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station.

Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani military pilot, is expected to travel to Tiangong on 25 November aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, alongside two Chinese astronauts, known as ‘taikonauts’.

According to recent reports, “My first [flight] not only represents myself, but also my country,” Ali told reporters in Mandarin on 24 November at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China. Ali has been training intensively in Beijing for the past seven months, including learning Mandarin. He said that he carried “the dream of 250 million Pakistani people” when he entered the training centre.

Sending an astronaut to space is “a huge step” for Pakistan’s space aspirations, indicates Wajiha Iqbal, a lunar scientist at the University of Münster in Germany. The partnership enables Pakistan to “do great science in space”, she adds.

The mission is also a milestone for China’s space programme. The country’s expanding capabilities now allow it to offer international partners opportunities that few countries can provide on their own, says Yuxuan Jia, who researches China’s foreign policy at the Center for China and Globalization, a think tank in Beijing. The launch signals China’s “aspirations to become a top space power”, Jia says.

Shenzhou-24 is expected to be carried into a low-Earth orbit by China’s Long March-2F rocket, which is scheduled to launch from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre at 08:18am local time on 25 November, stated Zhang Jingbo, a spokesperson of the China Manned Space Programme, at a press conference on 24 November. Shenzhou-24 is expected to automatically dock with Tiangong (which translates as ‘heavenly palace’) around 3.5 hours after reaching orbit.

Ali will stay on Tiangong for about a week before returning to Earth with two of the three taikonauts right now on the station.

China’s successful launch of Mars mission seals global era in deep-space exploration.

China’s successful launch of Mars mission seals global era in deep-space exploration.

It has been revealed that ali will board Shenzhou-24 as a payload specialist responsible mainly for scientific experiments rather than operating the spacecraft. The mission aims to host four biotechnology experiments developed by universities in Pakistan, Amer Gilani, an official at Pakistan’s space agency told newswire Reuters in September. Details about the research have not yet been made public.

In a recent development, according to Zhang, one goal of this mission is to establish a study of how the human body adapts to space flight. Zhu Yangzhu, an astronaut who entered Tiangong in May, will remain aboard the space station for another six months to allow for this experiment to take place, Zhang said.

Astronauts Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, Wu Yi and Tang Hongbo will travel to China's space station the Tiangong.Credit: CCTV+/VCG via Getty.

Tech Report: Physicists defy expectations by controlling the magnetic heart of a single atom

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (966 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, researchers at Delft University of Technology (The Netherlands) have accomplished something that physicists previously thought should not be possible.
  • In a recent development, the findings, published in Nature Communications, also present scientists with a fresh puzzle.
  • Sources indicate that atoms in magnetic metals such as iron and nickel behave like tiny magnets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, researchers at Delft University of Technology (The Netherlands) have accomplished something that physicists previously thought should not be possible. Using radio waves, they managed to directly control the magnetic spin of the nucleus inside a single atom. The unexpected result challenges existing assumptions about how atomic magnetism behaves and could eventually lead to latest ways of storing and retrieving quantum information.

In a recent development, the findings, published in Nature Communications, also present scientists with a fresh puzzle. Although the experiment demonstrated that this remarkable level of control is possible, researchers do not yet fully understand the mechanism that makes it work.

The Hidden Magnetism Inside Every Atom.

Sources indicate that atoms in magnetic metals such as iron and nickel behave like tiny magnets. However, the magnetism within an atom comes from different sources. Both electrons and, in some cases, the atomic nucleus possess a quantum property called spin, which can be thought of as a miniature magnetic compass needle.

Sources indicate that "By far the strongest magnetism comes from the electrons," says lead researcher Sander Otte. "But in some atoms, the nucleus also carries a spin. That spin is much weaker, but it is also much better shielded from the outside world.".

That protection makes nuclear spin especially interesting to quantum researchers. Because it is less exposed to disturbances from its surroundings, it could offer a promising way to preserve delicate quantum information.

Sources indicate that to investigate these tiny magnetic properties, Otte's team uses a specially modified scanning tunneling microscope. This powerful instrument allows the researchers to deliver electrical signals to individual atoms with extraordinary precision.

Until recently, their experiments concentrated primarily on electron spin because it is easier to detect and measure. The nucleus's magnetic spin could only be observed indirectly through a phenomenon known as the hyperfine interaction, which creates a subtle quantum connection between the spins of the electron and nucleus. This connection can cause the two spins to become slightly entangled, meaning their quantum states are linked.

An Atomic Experiment Produces an Unexpected Result.

In the latest study, lead author Hester Vennema and her colleagues took a different approach. They simultaneously applied two separate signals to a single atom, with one directed at the electron and the other at the nucleus.

By using these signals together, the researchers could investigate their effects independently. What happened next caught them by surprise.

Sources indicate that even when the electron and nuclear spins were largely disentangled, the team was still able to flip the orientation of the nucleus's magnetic spin. Based on their previous understanding, the nucleus should not have responded in this way.

Sources indicate that "According to our simple understanding, this should not really happen," indicates Otte. "The nuclear spin should not be sensitive at all to the electrical signals from a scanning tunneling microscope.".

The result suggests that the interaction between electrical signals and nuclear spin involves a mechanism that scientists have yet to fully explain.

Controlling Quantum Spins Like Guitar Strings.

Achieving this level of precision required the researchers to adapt a technique called double magnetic resonance so it could operate on a single atom. The method allowed them to manipulate the magnetic behavior of the atomic nucleus separately from that of an electron.

Magnetic resonance works by applying a wave signal at a carefully selected frequency to change the orientation of a magnetic spin. However, quantum mechanics restricts these changes to specific allowed transitions, meaning the frequency must be precisely matched to the spin being targeted.

Vennema compares the process to playing a musical instrument.

"You can compare it to the strings of a guitar," Vennema explains. "Each possible spin rotation is like a string with its own note. You have to play precisely the right note to make a particular string vibrate. The "notes" of a nuclear spin are a hundred to a thousand times lower than those of an electron spin.".

Sources indicate that in other words, electrons and atomic nuclei respond to very different frequencies, much as different guitar strings produce different musical notes. By tuning their signals to the appropriate frequencies, the scientists could address the two types of spin separately.

A Quantum Breakthrough With a Mystery Still to Solve.

The discovery could have important implications for the future of quantum information technology. Unlike conventional computers, which store information as bits representing either 0 or 1, quantum systems can use quantum states to encode information in more complex ways.

One major challenge is keeping those states stable long enough for information to be stored and retrieved reliably. Nuclear spins are attractive candidates for quantum memory because they are relatively well isolated from environmental interference.

In a recent development, the ability to control these spins directly could therefore open fresh possibilities for writing, storing, and reading quantum information. However, the findings represent an early experimental advance rather than a ready-to-use quantum memory technology.

It has been revealed that for now, one of the most key outcomes is the upcoming scientific mystery the experiment has revealed. The researchers have demonstrated an unexpected way to manipulate nuclear spin, but the physical mechanism responsible remains unclear.

Recent findings suggest that "Back to the drawing board, then," claims Otte. "That is really how science works. There is always something new left to figure out.".

Derek Hough healed through dance.

As the Dancing With the Stars judge looked back on the beginning of his path to becoming a professional dancer, he shared one of the darker chapters of his childhood with sister Julianne Hough while being raised in the suburbs of Salt Lake City, Utah.

"The neighborhood that we grew up in, we definitely just had some neighbors that weren't great. They pretty much terrorized my family in a lot of ways," Derek shared in his Nov. 23 documentary Symphony of Dance per USA Today, stating, "One of my neighbors was, for lack of a better word, just really inappropriate with me physically.".

In addition, the 41-year-old explained of the traumatic period, "They hung me up in a tree by my ankles, put a gun to my head, spat on me, hogtied me up in a field and left me there.".

According to recent reports, as such, enduring the abuse led to "a lot of emotion" for the then-12-year-old, who was raised alongside his DWTS costar as well as their older siblings Sharee, 49, Marabeth, 45 and Katherine, 44, by parents Bruce Hough and Mariann Heaton in the Mormon community. Julianne has previously shared that a painful part of her upbringing came at the hands of a neighbor in their cul-de-sac who she said sexually abused her at age 4.

According to recent reports, "I just didn't understand where I was going," Derek said in the Hulu project about his reaction to the harmful treatment. "I was kind of left to my own devices.".

And at first, the trauma pushed the choreographer further away from his future as a ballroom pro.

Sources indicate that as he detailed, "I was a 12-year-old. I would skip school. I would skip dance. I wouldn't go. My dad was at work, and my mom was off, and [I was] just floating around with no direction.".

Fortunately, Derek was "relieved" when he met mentors Corky Ballas and Shirley Ballas—parents of DWTS coach Mark Ballas—who soon moved Derek, and eventually Julianne, to London to attend drama academy Italia Conti Academy of Theatre Arts.

"Moving away was great because I was getting away from something," he noted. "I was leaving this wounded boy, and I was gonna go become this success. I was gonna go work hard and achieve things and overcome things.".

According to recent reports, and the Emmy winner did exactly that, noting how the professional performers in his new world made him realize at the time, "This is what I want to do. I want to be like these guys.".

Recent findings suggest that julianne alluded to her siblings undergoing hardship similar to her own on The Jamie Kern Lima Show Aug. 15 while telling her story, noting, "By the way, I'm not the only one in my family that had gone through similar things, so that was a very challenging thing to come to terms with.".

Read on for a closer look at the Hough family tree.

The Hough family patriarch is originally from Coeur d’Alene, Idaho, and met future wife Mariann Heaton on the ballroom team at Ricks College (now Brigham Young University-Idaho).

Sources indicate that bruce and Mariann—both from Mormon families and the children of ballroom-dancing parents—settled in Salt Lake City. There he worked as a communications executive and co-founded supplement maker Nutraceutical Corporation, which, according to Deseret News, reached a valuation of $300 million under his watch before it was sold in 2017.

Bruce also ventured into politics, serving two terms as state Republican Party chair and running for congress in 2023.

While he didn't win that race, he told Deseret News at the time that he was running for his family's future. "I’ve got 10 kids, I’ve got 22 grandkids and growing," he explained. "And I really feel that America’s promise is in jeopardy for those grandkids especially.".

Of his most famous offspring, he quipped, "I never thought that those dance lessons would pay off,” noting that he took the most pride in hearing from others that son Derek Hough and daughter Julianne Hough were some of the "kindest people…in the entertainment business.”.

In addition to Derek and Julianne, Bruce shares daughters Sharee Hough Selman, Marabeth Poole and Katherine Hough with Mariann. After they divorced in the late 1990s, he married Debra Francom Hough, also a parent of five.

Mariann grew up in Idaho Falls with three brothers.

She and Bruce were in the process of divorcing when Julianne and Derek, then 10 and 13, moved to London to attend the Italia Conti Academy of Theatre Arts.

Their leaving was "devastating," Mariann recalled on a 2019 episode of The Minds Gym podcast. But they wanted to dance and, she explained, "The biggest thing that kept me going is that I grew up feeling very dominated over and controlled. Love my parents, but that was like a generational thing.".

However, she added, "I'm grateful for that now because…it made me sway to I love having free agency." It was also "so key" for her to pass that on to her kids, she mentioned, and "all of them are so not afraid to go travel and do all these things.".

Mariann, now based in Franklin, Tenn., is a painter and has credited husband Aaron Nelson for supporting and encouraging her work as an artist.

Sharee married husband Mark Selman when she was 19 and they share six kids.

The eldest of Bruce and Mariann's brood danced at Ballet West in Utah and these days runs her own fitness business, Hough Werks, teaching yoga and dance.

Her "dynamic" firstborn "just came into this world with a lot of energy," Mariann stated on The Minds Gym. Sharee's "little mind was just going all the time, just super creative" and "self-motivated.".

Moreover, with 11 years between Sharee and her youngest sister, "Julianne thinks she has two moms.".

Marabeth is "just a beautiful spirit" who "loves her own space," Mariann said of her second child, and she "puts on these little retreats in Nashville for women.".

She left Utah for Music City to "be a country star," baby sister Julianne shared on the Not Skinny but Not Fat podcast in September 2025, and now makes the most of her positive energy as a realtor and holistic health coach, as well as a singer-songwriter.

Marabeth married Michael Poole in 2002 and they live in Nashville with son Aidan.

Daughter Katherine, a mother of three, "just makes you smile," Mariann noted on The Minds Gym, "and she's just real.".

According to recent reports, the esthetician was in a relationship with Tony Schnur before his death from brain cancer in 2023. "It’s unfair that I found my soulmate, my best friend, my partner in life, only to lose you too soon," Katherine posted on Instragram in February 2025, marking the second anniversary of his passing. "I miss you every day.".

But Katherine has persevered, Julianne gushing on Not Skinny But Not Fat, "She has three beautiful daughters and she has all these activities and she intends all these things, and I'm in awe of her.".

And on Sept. 24, 2025, Katherine shared that she had found love again, writing on Instagram alongside a montage of sweet photos, "After walking through so much loss and heartache, I never imagined I’d find this kind of love again. Chris is the man I prayed for, kind, generous, loving, patient, and such a gift not only to me but to my girls.".

It has been revealed that born May 17, 1985, Derek joined Dancing With the Stars as a pro in 2007. He won the Mirrorball Trophy a record six times and is a four-time Emmy winner for choreography.

After his last competitive turn around the floor in 2016, Derek returned to DWTS as a fulltime judge in 2020.

He met fellow dancer Hayley Erbert in 2015 and, after navigating some "insane obstacles," as he put it on Couple Things With Shawn Johnson and Andrew East, they got married in August 2023.

As a couple they powered through Hayley's life-threatening health scare, a brain hemorrhage that required emergency surgery just four months after their wedding, and in July 2025 they announced they were expecting their first child together.

It has been revealed that posting a photo of dad Bruce dancing at his and Hayley's wedding, Derek wrote on Facebook in April 2024, "Smart, kind and thoughtful. I hope to be as good as a father as he has been to his family.".

In a recent development, the baby of the Hough family was born July 20,1988. She joined DWTS in 2007 along with Derek and proceeded to win her first two seasons on the show.

Recent findings suggest that she left in 2009 to pursue acting and scored a breakthrough role in 2010's Burlesque (though her substantial-screen debut was actually playing an unnamed Hogwarts student in 2001's Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone) before scoring the lead in the 2011 Footloose remake. Julianne returned to the ballroom as a judge from 2014 to 2017, winning an Emmy for choreography along the way, and has cohosted DWTS with Alfonso Ribeiro since 2023.

Julianne married Brooks Laich in 2017 but they split up in 2020, eventually finalizing their divorce in 2022.

She remarked on The Jamie Kern Lima Show in 2024 that going through a divorce gave her a chance to "reconnect" with her mom and dad, and they "highlighted up" for her.

It has been revealed that "I needed that," Julianne explained. "I reclaimed my parental relationship with them and I got to be the kid and they got to take care of me. And that was the most healing [thing].".

Reflecting on her and Derek becoming the stars of the family, Julianne stated on Not Skinny But Not Fat that there was "no jealousy" between their other siblings, "but there is a sadness that maybe there wasn't an opportunity for them to experience it.".

Sharee, Marabeth and Katherine are "so, so, so happy," Julianne continued. "They have great lives, and they love their life. But we had an opportunity that they didn't have, and it's hard.”.

It has been revealed that and while she and Derek have a special connection, "they were super close as sisters growing up,” Julianne mentioned. “So, I didn't get to have the closeness of sisters and that bond. [And] they have marriages and kids and I don't have that experience.".

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, all five siblings "get along really well," Mariann remarked on The Minds Gym. "I think the hard part is being away from each other, because there is some kind of a synergy when they all get together.".
